    23	  \label{L:positive-raw-embedding}
    24	  For any real Hilbert space $G$ there is a bounded map $J_G:L^2(I;G) \to
    25	  H_t\otimes G$ with
    26	  \begin{equation}\label{E:positive-bochner-inclusion}
    27	    \|J_GF\|^2
    28	    =\int_{I^2}K(s,t)\langle F(s),F(t)\rangle_G\ud s\ud t
    29	    \le K_0\|F\|_{L^2(I;G)}^2,\qquad K_0=\frac{2^a}{1-a}.
    30	  \end{equation}
    31	  The natural inclusion puts every $\Psi \in \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}$ in
    32	  $H_I$, with
    33	  \begin{equation}\label{E:positive-raw-mean}
    34	    \|\Psi\|_{H_I}^2=v_\Psi,\qquad
    35	    \mathcal{T}_R\Psi(s)=B_E(m_Rh_{\Psi,s})\quad\hbox{a.e. }s.
    36	  \end{equation}
    37	  For each fixed smooth $\Psi$ the right side gives a canonical version for
    38	  every $R \ge 1$ and every $s \in I$.
    39	\end{lemma}

    24	  \label{L:occupation-raw-square}

    26	  \[
    27	    \langle Q(f),Q(h)\rangle_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}
    28	    =B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2),\qquad
    29	    \|Q(f)\|^2=A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f).

    35	    \langle\Psi,\rho_g\rangle_{H_I}
    36	    =\int_I\int_{\R^d}h_{\Psi,s}(x)g_s(x)^2\ud x\ud s

    64	\begin{lemma}[Global regularity of the original mean]
    65	  \label{L:variational-global-mean}
    66	  Every mixed time and space derivative of $h_s$ is globally bounded in space,
    67	  uniformly on compact time intervals. In particular, for $I = [0,1]$ there are
    68	  finite constants $M,C_\Psi$ such that
    69	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-global-mean}
    70	    0\le h_s(x)\le M,\qquad
    71	    \|h_s-h_t\|_\infty\le C_\Psi|s-t|,
    72	    \qquad s,t\in I.
    73	  \end{equation}
    74	\end{lemma}
    75	
    76	\begin{proof}
    77	  Extend $\Psi$ by zero in time; its compact support inside $(0,1)$ makes this a
    78	  smooth extension. For any mixed derivative $D\Psi$, a fixed $\epsilon > 0$ and
    79	  compactness of its common spatial support give $|D\Psi(t,x)| \le
    80	  C_Dp_\epsilon(x)$ for all $t,x$. Here the heat kernel has a positive minimum
    81	  on that support. Lemma~\ref{L:variational-heat-envelope} consequently bounds
    82	  $\Gamma*|D\Psi(t,\cdot)|$ uniformly in $t,x$. Ordinary local differentiation
    83	  against the Radon measure gives the corresponding derivatives of the
    84	  convolution. After the change $r = s-t$,
    85	  \[
    86	    h_s(x)=\int_\R |r|^{-a}
    87	    (\Gamma*\Psi(s-r,\cdot))(x)\ud r.
    88	  \]
    89	  For $s$ in a compact interval the relevant $r$ lie in a fixed bounded
    90	  interval. The preceding global bound times $|r|^{-a}$ is integrable since $a <
    91	  1$. Every derivative thus falls on the smooth test and passes through the
    92	  integral by dominated convergence, with the claimed global spatial bounds.
    93	  Nonnegativity follows from positive kernels. The bounded time derivative
    94	  proves the Lipschitz estimate. No directional decay of the mean has been
    95	  inferred. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:variational-global-mean}.
    96	\end{proof}

    98	\begin{proposition}[The unmasked Rayleigh rate]
    99	  \label{P:variational-unmasked-rate}
   100	  On complex $L^2(\R^d)$, the operator $H_s = -\Delta-h_s$ is self-adjoint on
   101	  $H^2$, with form domain $H^1$ and form $q_s(f) = \|\nabla f\|_2^2-\int
   102	  h_s|f|^2$. Its spectral bottom $E_s$ is uniformly negative on $I$. The
   103	  positive rate $\lambda_{\Psi,s} = \sqrt{-E_s}$ satisfies
   104	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-real-rayleigh}
   105	    \lambda_{\Psi,s}^2
   106	    =\sup_{\substack{f\in H^1(\R^d;\R)\\\|f\|_2=1}}
   107	    \left(\int h_sf^2-\|\nabla f\|_2^2\right).
   108	  \end{equation}
   109	  It is Lipschitz on $I$, and $I_\Psi: = \int_0^1\lambda_{\Psi,s}\ud s$ is
   110	  positive and finite. No eigenstate at the unmasked bottom is asserted.
   111	\end{proposition}
   270	\begin{proposition}[Intrinsic variational lower bounds]
   271	  \label{P:variational-positive-scores}
   272	  For $c > 0$, the set of variational values
   273	  $\{cI_\Psi-v_\Psi/2:\Psi\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}\}$ is nonempty and
   274	  bounded above. Its finite real supremum $S_c^{\mathrm{pos}}$ is positive and
   275	  satisfies

   282	  auxiliary variational value; no first-moment or source-constant identification

   284	\end{proposition}
   458	\begin{lemma}[Exact Rayleigh tail bound]\label{L:tube-rayleigh-tail}
   459	  Suppose $G$ is Borel and $G(r) \le A_0+Cr^\nu$, $C \ge 0$, $1 < \nu < 2$. If
   460	  $M > 0$ and $4C \le M^{2-\nu}$, then
   461	  \begin{equation}\label{E:tube-rayleigh-tail}
   462	    \int_M^\infty\frac r\delta
   463	    e^{(G(r)-r^2/2)/\delta}\ud r
   464	    \le4e^{(A_0-M^2/4)/\delta}.
   465	  \end{equation}

   468	\end{lemma}

  2472	\begin{lemma}[Gaussian cutoff form bound]\label{L:fock-form}
  2473	  Retain the covariance and $R_\alpha$ of Section~\ref{S:static-phase}. Fix
  2474	  $\epsilon > 0$. Represent the smoothed real field on independent standard
  2475	  Gaussian coordinates as $W_\epsilon(x) = \sum_{i\ge1}g_i e_i(x)$ in
  2476	  $L^2(\Omega)$. Let $P_N$ be projection onto Gaussian Hermite degrees at most
  2477	  $N$, and $S_b$ spatial Fourier projection onto $|\eta| \le b$. For finite $m$,
  2478	  on their joint range set
  2479	  \[
  2480	    B_{N,m,b}=P_NS_b\Big(\sum_{i=1}^m g_i M_{e_i}\Big)S_bP_N,\qquad
  2481	    A_\rho=\rho^2-\Delta .
  2482	  \]
  2483	  These are bounded selfadjoint operators and, uniformly in $\epsilon,m,b$,
  2484	  \begin{equation}\label{E:fock-sandwich}
  2485	    \|A_\rho^{-1/2}B_{N,m,b}A_\rho^{-1/2}\|
  2486	    \le d_N\rho^{\alpha/2-2},\qquad
  2487	    d_N=2\sqrt{N+1}\sqrt{R_\alpha}.
  2488	  \end{equation}
  2489	\end{lemma}
  2490	
  2491	\begin{proof}
  2492	  Choose an orthonormal basis of the real isonormal space, which is separable,
  2493	  and write $e_i(x) = \E[W_\epsilon(x)g_i]$. Then $\sum_i e_i(x)^2 =
  2494	  \Gamma_\epsilon(0) = :v_\epsilon$, and $|e_i(x)| \le \sqrt{v_\epsilon}$. Thus,
  2495	  each multiplication $M_{e_i}$ is bounded and selfadjoint. Put $H_i =
  2496	  A_\rho^{-1/2}M_{e_i}A_\rho^{-1/2}$ on spatial $L^2$. Gaussian isometry and
  2497	  spatial Plancherel give
  2498	  \[
  2499	    \sum_i\|H_i f\|_2^2
  2500	    =\frac1{(2\pi)^3}\int
  2501	    \frac{|\widehat{f}(\eta)|^2}{\rho^2+|\eta|^2}
  2502	    J_{\rho,\epsilon}(\eta)\ud\eta,\qquad
  2503	    J_{\rho,\epsilon}(\eta)
  2504	    =\int\frac{e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2}\mu(\ud\xi)}
  2505	    {\rho^2+|\eta+\xi|^2}.
  2506	  \]
  2507	  This is the covariance calculation for $A_\rho^{-1/2}W_\epsilon
  2508	  A_\rho^{-1/2}f$. By Lemma~\ref{L:phase-contractions}, $J_{\rho,\epsilon} \le
  2509	  R_\alpha\rho^{\alpha-2}$. Therefore, $\sum_i H_i^2 \le
  2510	  R_\alpha\rho^{\alpha-4}I$ in quadratic forms. Finite sums have the same upper
  2511	  bound. Compression to $S_b$ preserves it: for selfadjoint $H_i$,
  2512	  $(S_bH_iS_b)^2 \le S_bH_i^2S_b$ on its range. Both row and column variances
  2513	  are the same, since these operators are selfadjoint.
  2514	
  2515	  For completeness, use normalized Hermite polynomials, so multiplication by
  2516	  $g_i$ is $a_i^*+a_i$, with $g_i h_k =
  2517	  \sqrt{k_i+1}\,h_{k+e_i}+\sqrt{k_i}\,h_{k-e_i}$. On degree $k$, the row map
  2518	  $(v_i)\mapsto\sum_i a_i^*v_i$ has norm $\sqrt{k+1}$: its product with its
  2519	  adjoint is $\sum_i a_i^*a_i = (k+1)I$ on degree $k+1$. Composing with the
  2520	  column of spatial operators $S_bH_iS_b$ bounds the creation part by
  2521	  $\sqrt{k+1}\sqrt{R_\alpha}\rho^{(\alpha-4)/2}$. Distinct input degrees have
  2522	  orthogonal output degrees. The annihilation part is its adjoint, with the same
  2523	  bound after truncation. Adding them on degrees at most $N$ proves
  2524	  \eqref{E:fock-sandwich}. Boundedness of $-\Delta$ on $S_b$ is explicit; no
  2525	  infinite-frequency operator theorem was used. This proves
  2526	  Lemma~\ref{L:fock-form}.
  2527	\end{proof}

  2531	\begin{lemma}[Exact cutoffs for finite Gaussian words]\label{L:finite-word-cutoff}
  2532	  Let $g_{ij}$, $1 \le i \le M$, $1 \le j \le m_i$, be independent standard real
  2533	  Gaussian coordinates, grouped by color $i$, and let $\mathscr{X}$ be a complex
  2534	  Hilbert space. On Gaussian polynomials with coefficients in $\mathscr{X}$ set
  2535	  \[
  2536	    J_i=\sum_{j=1}^{m_i}M_{g_{ij}}\otimes K_{ij},

  2539	  bounded operators acting only on $\mathscr{X}$. Fix a word $i_1,\ldots,i_n$,
  2540	  and let $r_i$ be the number of its occurrences of color $i$. If $N_i \ge r_i$

  2542	  every $v \in \mathscr{X}$,
  2543	  \begin{equation}\label{E:finite-word-cutoff}

  2546	      (PJ_{i_1}P)(I\otimes F_0)(1\otimes v)\\

  2548	      J_{i_1}(I\otimes F_0)(1\otimes v).

  3600	\begin{lemma}[The finite terminal-chain Wick formula]\label{L:terminal-wick}
  3601	  Let $\mathcal{W}(s,y)$ be a centered real Gaussian field on $[0,T]\times\R^d$,
  3602	  $d = 1,2,3$, with covariance $\mathcal{K}(s,y;r,z)$. Suppose that $V =
  3603	  \sup_{s,y}\E|\mathcal{W}(s,y)|^2 < \infty$, and that the field is jointly
  3604	  continuous in mean square on each open cell of a finite partition of $[0,T]$,
  3605	  times $\R^d$. Define $Y_0 = 1$ and
  3606	  \[
  3607	    Y_n(T,x)=\int\prod_{j=1}^n\mathcal{W}(s_j,y_j)
  3608	    \,\mathsf{g}_n^{T,x}(\ud\boldsymbol s,\ud\boldsymbol y).
  3609	  \]
  3610	  These Bochner integrals exist in $L^2(\Omega)$ and satisfy
  3611	  \begin{equation}\label{E:terminal-term-majorant}
  3612	    \|Y_n(T,x)\|_2
  3613	    \le\sqrt{(2n-1)!!}\,V^{n/2}\frac{T^{2n}}{(2n)!},
  3614	    \qquad n\ge1.
  3615	  \end{equation}
  3616	  For $m+n = 2k$, concatenate $\boldsymbol\tau =
  3617	  (s_1,\ldots,s_m,r_1,\ldots,r_n)$ and $\boldsymbol\eta =
  3618	  (y_1,\ldots,y_m,z_1,\ldots,z_n)$. Then
  3619	  \begin{equation}\label{E:terminal-wick-formula}
  3620	    \E[Y_m(T,x)Y_n(T,x)]
  3621	    =\sum_{D\in\Pi_k}\mathcal{T}_{m,n,D}^{\mathcal{K}}(T,x),
  3622	  \end{equation}
  3623	  where, with both chains terminating at $(T,x)$,
  3624	  \begin{equation}\label{E:terminal-pairing-integral}
  3625	    \begin{split}
  3626	      \mathcal{T}_{m,n,D}^{\mathcal{K}}
  3627	      ={}&\int_{[0,T]^m_<\times[0,T]^n_<}
  3628	      \ud\boldsymbol s\,\ud\boldsymbol r
  3629	      \int_{(\R^d)^m\times(\R^d)^n}\\
  3630	      &\quad\times\prod_{j=1}^m
  3631	      G_{s_{j+1}-s_j}(y_{j+1}-\ud y_j)
  3632	      \prod_{j=1}^n
  3633	      G_{r_{j+1}-r_j}(z_{j+1}-\ud z_j)\\
  3634	      &\quad\times\prod_{\{a,b\}\in D}

  3636	    \end{split}
  3637	  \end{equation}

  3645	\end{lemma}
  7222	\begin{lemma}[Type of a positive coefficient series]\label{L:positive-series-type}
  7223	  Let $\nu \ge 1$, $c_k \ge 0$, $c_0 = 1$, and suppose $F(z) =
  7224	  \sum_{k\ge0}c_kz^k < \infty$ for every $z \ge 0$. If
  7225	  \[
  7226	    \tau=\limsup_{z\to\infty}z^{-1/\nu}\log F(z)<\infty,

  7228	  then

  7232	  \end{equation}

  2288	\begin{lemma}[A complex phase bound]\label{L:complex-phase}
  2289	  Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space, $A_0$ a bounded nonnegative selfadjoint
  2290	  operator, and $B$ a bounded selfadjoint operator. Write $A_\rho = \rho^2+A_0$.
  2291	  Suppose that, for $0 < a < 1$ and $d > 0$,
  2292	  \begin{equation}\label{E:abstract-sandwich}
  2293	    \|A_\rho^{-1/2}BA_\rho^{-1/2}\|\le d\rho^{a-2},
  2294	    \qquad \rho>0.
  2295	  \end{equation}
  2296	  Put
  2297	  \[
  2298	    I_a=\int_0^\infty s^{-1/2}(1+s)^{(a-3)/2}\ud s,\qquad
  2299	    \delta_a=\min\{1/4,\pi/(8I_a)\}.
  2300	  \]
  2301	  For $\lambda > 0$ and $|z| \le \delta_a\lambda^{2-a}/d$, let $L = A_0-zB$. The
  2302	  phase propagator of $u''+Lu = 0$ satisfies
  2303	  \begin{equation}\label{E:complex-phase-bound}
  2304	    \|\mathcal{M}_z(h)\|_{X_\lambda\to X_\lambda}
  2305	    \le100e^{2\lambda h},\qquad
  2306	    \|(f,g)\|_{X_\lambda}^2
  2307	    =\|f\|^2+\|A_\lambda^{-1/2}g\|^2,\quad h\ge0.
  2308	  \end{equation}
  2309	  The constant is independent of $H$, $\|A_0\|$ and $\|B\|$.
  2310	\end{lemma}
  2828	\begin{lemma}[Dimension-independent Gaussian contractions]
  2829	  \label{L:interval-contractions}
  2830	  Uniformly in positive spatial smoothing and in finite Gaussian-mode and
  2831	  spatial Fourier-band cutoffs,
  2832	  \begin{equation}\label{E:interval-column}
  2833	    \sum_m\|A_\rho^{-1/2}M_{e_m}f\|_2^2
  2834	    \le R_\alpha\rho^{\alpha-2}\|f\|_2^2.
  2835	  \end{equation}
  2836	  Here $W_\epsilon(x) = \sum_m g_me_m(x)$ is an orthonormal-coordinate
  2837	  representation of $W(p_\epsilon(x-\cdot))$, whose covariance is
  2838	  $\Gamma_\epsilon = p_{2\epsilon}*\Gamma$. Consequently, on a Gaussian color
  2839	  that is initially in its vacuum, the phase insertion
  2840	  $(u,v)\mapsto(0,W_\epsilon u)$ has norm at most
  2841	  $\sqrt{R_\alpha}\rho^{(\alpha-2)/2}$ into its Gaussian $L^2$ phase. With
  2842	  Hermite degree of this color truncated at $N$, its sandwiched field has
  2843	  operator norm at most
  2844	  \begin{equation}\label{E:interval-fock}
  2845	    2\sqrt{N+1}\sqrt{R_\alpha}\rho^{\alpha/2-2}.
  2846	  \end{equation}
  2847	  Both statements remain valid tensoring with any other Hilbert factor.
  2848	\end{lemma}
  2899	\begin{lemma}[Complex sums and changing phase weights]
  2900	  \label{L:interval-complex}
  2901	  Let $A_0$ be bounded, nonnegative and selfadjoint, and let $V$ be bounded on
  2902	  the same complex Hilbert space. Write $A_\rho = \rho^2+A_0$. The complex phase
  2903	  conclusion of Lemma~\ref{L:complex-phase} holds for $L = A_0-V$ whenever $V$
  2904	  is bounded, not necessarily selfadjoint,
  2905	  \[
  2906	    \|A_\rho^{-1/2}VA_\rho^{-1/2}\|\le D\rho^{a-2},\qquad \rho>0,
  2907	    \quad 0<a<1,\quad D\le\delta_a\Lambda^{2-a}.
  2908	  \]
  2909	  Its bound is $100e^{2\Lambda h}$ in $X_\Lambda$. If a piecewise-constant
  2910	  potential is the sum of connected-interval fields, assign a positive weight
  2911	  $\omega_i$ to each field present and put $\Lambda(t) =
  2912	  \lambda+\sum_i\omega_i\mathbf1_{I_i}(t)$. The total loss from changing between
  2913	  these phase norms, starting and ending in $X_\lambda$, is at most
  2914	  \begin{equation}\label{E:interval-metric}
  2915	    \prod_i(1+\omega_i/\lambda).
  2916	  \end{equation}
  2917	\end{lemma}

  3403	  There is $C = C(\alpha,\alpha_0,L,c)$ such that, for real Schwartz phase $v$,

    30	\begin{lemma}[Free wave form and compact Young baseline]
    31	  \label{L:symplectic-free}
    32	  There is a bounded isometric skew-adjoint $J_E$ on $E$, with $J_E^2 = -I$,
    33	  such that
    34	  \[
    35	    \omega(z,w)=\langle z,J_Ew\rangle_E
    36	    =\langle u,g\rangle_{H^{1/2},H^{-1/2}}
    37	    -\langle f,v\rangle_{H^{1/2},H^{-1/2}},
    38	    \quad z=(u,v),\quad w=(f,g).
    39	  \]
    40	  The free group preserves $\omega$. For bounded real smooth $b$, the force
    41	  $B(b)(u,v) = (0,bu)$ obeys $\omega(B(b)z,w)+\omega(z,B(b)w) = 0$.
    42	
    43	  Let $1/2 < \theta < 1$ and let $X \in C^\theta([0,T];\mathcal{K}(E))$ start at
    44	  zero, with $U_X$ its left Young evolution. Then
    45	  \begin{equation}\label{E:symplectic-compact-young-baseline}
    46	    U_X(t,s)-I\in\mathcal{K}(E),\qquad
    47	    \|S_E(t)U_X(t,s)S_E(-s)\|
    48	    \ge\|S_E(t-s)\|\ge1,\qquad 0\le s\le t\le T .
    49	  \end{equation}
    50	  More generally, for finitely many such paths $X_j$ starting at zero on $[0,B]$
    51	  and lengths $0 \le \ell_j \le B$, put $P_j = S_E(\ell_j)U_{X_j}(\ell_j,0)$.
    52	  Then
    53	  \begin{equation}\label{E:symplectic-compact-product-baseline}
    54	    P_N\cdots P_0-S_E\Big(\sum_{j=0}^N\ell_j\Big)\in\mathcal{K}(E),
    55	    \qquad
    56	    \|P_N\cdots P_0\|
    57	    \ge\left\|S_E\Big(\sum_{j=0}^N\ell_j\Big)\right\|\ge1 .
    58	  \end{equation}
    59	  These norm bounds require neither Gaussian nor Hamiltonian operator paths.
    60	\end{lemma}
